newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-CBI to show UK manufacturers more hopefuL.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-CBI to show UK manufacturers more hopefuL.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry's quarterly trends survey is expected to show Britain's manufacturers are feeling more optimistic, analysts say.
But the bald figures may reveal the balance of manufacturing firms reporting improved business confidence is no higher than in the CBI's last quarterly survey in July.

"Our forecast is that the confidence figure will be stable at eight percent which, given the usual seasonal patterns, would imply a strong underlying figure," said Michael Saunders, UK economist at Salomon Brothers.

Saunders said the July to October quarter has generally been a poor one for British industry. On average, the CBI survey's business confidence component has fallen by five percentage points between the July and October surveys, he said.
In the July survey, a positive balance of eight percent of manufacturing firms said they were more optimistic about their general business situation than four months previously.
The latest survey is due at 1030 GMT on Tuesday.
"The CBI survey should show the manufacturing sector continuing to benefit from the consumer-led recovery," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"In particular, we would would look for a further improvement in order books, the output balance already indicates a move to above-trend growth."
The July trends survey showed a positive balance of 18 percent of firms polled expected new orders to improve. Tuesday's figures will show whether their confidence was justified.
Similarly, a balance of 22 percent of companies expected output to improve, when asked in July. Saunders forecast that figure will ease back to 20 percent this time.

Dharshini David, economist at HSBC Markets, said recent surveys from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply and the British Chambers of Commerce pointed to better economic conditions for industry, and rising confidence.

"The business optimism balance of the CBI industrial trends survey rose in July for the first time since April 1995, and there is good reason to believe that it will continue to be upbeat this quarter," she said.
This month's survey will be keenly watched to see if the mountainous stockpiles of unsold goods, which have blighted manufacturing output, are now declining significantly.
"With demand strengthening, a sustained recovery in output seems likely in the next few months," David said.
But good news for exports may prove harder to come by.
David said the weakness of European markets and the strength of the pound, up eight percent on the mark since early August, were making life tough for exporters.
In September's monthly trends survey, a negative of 11 percent of firms said they were more optimistic about exports than they were a year ago.
On the positive side for the gilt market, the CBI survey is unlikely to show a meaningful increase in inflation pressures.
Saunders forecast a balance of five percent of firms in the October survey will say they expect prices to rise. In the September monthly trends survey, the balance was zero.

"But the prices guide usually rises between September and October, with an average gain of five percent," he said. "We expect a similar rise this year, implying little change in the seasonally adjusted series."
